paper.quote: At high SNR levels (e.g., 30 dB), where channel estimation errors are negligible, the CNN–LSTM performance (2.77°) and the closed-form optimum (2.70°) fall within the 95% confidence interval ( ± 0.08°), confirming that the model converges to the information-theoretic floor of the system under ideal conditions.

At high SNR (e.g., 30 dB), the CNN–LSTM performance (2.77°) and the closed-form optimum (2.70°) overlap within the 95% confidence interval (± 0.08°), confirming that the proposed model successfully reaches the information-theoretic floor of the system under ideal propagation conditions.

items.contradiction: The RMSE metric (Eq. 9) is measured against θ_true, and θ_true IS the closed-form solution (Eq. 8; p9 Sec 4.1 'optimal phase labels are computed via Equation (8)'; ZIP/RIS_dataset_large_2D.m:100). Under perfect CSI the closed-form vs its own label has RMSE = 0° by definition. The text conditions on 'high SNR ... channel estimation errors are negligible' but gives no CSI-error level, no noise model and no definition under which the closed form would score 2.70°. Also the paper's own CSI model (Sec 5.6.2) is additive noise on F,G, not an SNR-dependent estimate; no code exists for it.

paper.quote: 1. Discrete Phase Quantization. Quantizing to 2^b levels (b ∈ {1, 2, 3} bits): 1-bit → 4.12°, 2-bit → 3.08°, 3-bit → 2.81° RMSE (continuous: 2.77°). Two-bit quantization recovers near-continuous performance, consistent with [38].

items.note: UPL/a7225990-README_GitHub_3.md:37-41 lists quantization/quant_aware_train_updated.m, quant_aware_train_3bit.m, quant_aware_test_updated.m, quant_aware_test_3bit.m — none of these files exist in ZIP, REPO, UPL or ORIJ. Same README :120-126 gives only '<4% (3-bit)', '<10% (2-bit)' and no 1-bit. Definitional gap: RMSE of a b-bit quantised phase vs a continuous label has a floor of (2π/2^b)/√12: 1-bit ≈ 52°, 2-bit ≈ 26°, 3-bit ≈ 13°, unless the RMSE is defined differently (e.g. vs a quantised label) — the paper does not say which.

source.727K: Analytic sum in paper Sec 3.5 (p9) is internally consistent (13,440+148,224+565,696 = 727,360) and is also hard-coded in UPL/f2d4df3b-scalability_analysis.m:57 (PARAMS_cnn(1) = 727360) and its per-block constants at :122-123. It does NOT match either code model: theta_NN_multioutput.m (ZIP lines 56-77) = 161,794 learnables (no FC256/128/64 block); train_cnn_lstm.py (ZIP lines 93-116, N=32) = 822,976 (PyTorch double LSTM bias, second LSTM 128 not 64, extra lstm_proj and a 4th FC). Counts: step3_arith_check.json params. (aisy_paket/README_TR.md item 7 quotes 162,562 for the MATLAB stack — 768 more than this count; not reconciled here.)
